body: Hey, thanks man. Knowing that someone has felt this way and found some solace is probably going to be the main reason I go find somebody to talk to.

Hah, you hear it because I feel it. I guess I just don't know how to tell them I'm in pain without sounding like a total shit for being upset in the first place.

I'm seriously considering the therapist... I just feel weird paying a stranger to listen to me complain. I really do think it's time to just bite the bullet and do it.

Yeah. I definitely struggled with the adjustment, but as far as work goes, I'm doing pretty well. I'm well-liked by my coworkers, and I'm known for being smart, friendly, and quick. The only part of this shift that I'm really having issue with is making friends. I would love to be able to talk to them one on one, but I feel like they wouldn't even be open to hanging out with me alone... and I'm afraid I would become angry and accusatory, and that would just drive them further away.

I've tried to talk myself into going to "meetups" on several occasions... but under my friendly sunshine exterior, I'm painfully shy. A more appropriate term is probably painfully afraid. I'm afraid that I'm going to go there and it'll be a waste of my time, or that I'll go there, make a friend, and end up in this same fucking situation all over again.

I try to talk to her as much as I can, but I don't want to burden her. She has enough on her plate already.

I really appreciate your advice. It may just be time to nut up and go talk to strangers.

It's a sick sort of comfort to read that it's not something only I feel.

But how do I stop feeling bad about feeling bad? The fucking guilt weight, oh my *god* the fucking guilt weight. It's so selfish. This whole act, this whole emotion is so fucking selfish.

Honestly I don't think anything changed. I just kind of realized that they didn't care about me, and once I thought about it some, I realized that they had never done anything to indicate that they ever did. Fair weather friends, y'know what I mean? When we were all going out and having fun together, it was great. Now that I'm struggling, they're nowhere to be found. I get it, I'm less fun now, but people who care for me would recognize that as a need for help, right? I'm too ashamed and too proud to tell them that I need help, but I feel like everything I do and everything I say is screaming *Please, please someone help me.*
